notes.title: 8 Years After Release: “Gold Rush! 2” Gets an Update!
notes.content: [p]More than eight years after its original launch, Sunlight Games has released a brand-new update for Gold Rush! 2. Version 1.0.5 is now available for PC via Steam. Updates for the boxed PC version as well as iOS and Android will follow shortly.[/p][p]The update includes minor bug fixes and addresses compatibility issues with a few rare processor types. Several technical improvements enhance stability and overall game compatibility.[/p][p]Key changes in version 1.0.5:[/p][list][*][p]The game engine has been updated to the latest version.[/p][/*][*][p]The save system has been completely rebuilt. A built-in converter detects old savegames at startup, backs them up, and converts them automatically. If any issues occur with the converted saves, players are encouraged to contact the development team via the website.[/p][/*][*][p]There were issues starting the game on a few processors after a Windows driver update. This has been fixed.[/p][/*][*][p]New savegames now use dedicated file extensions. An issue with a Steam-generated file in the save directory has been fixed. Cloud Save functionality will be re-enabled soon![/p][/*][*][p]A rare scene transition bug, previously requiring a workaround, has been resolved.[/p][/*][*][p]The mouse cursor is now properly locked within the game screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Various minor bugs have been fixed.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Gold Rush! 2 update to 1.0.3 released for PC!
notes.content:
A first update to version 1.0.3 for Gold Rush! 2, the sequel to Gold Rush! Anniversary, is available on Steam. The update fixes some small issues and adds some texts and voices.

Here is the changelog:
- Minor graphics issues fixed
- Some words was mispronounced in the voices, they was recorded new
- Before the first train-quest, there was a mistake with the text
- The texts for the robbery in the train was changed
- fixed some layer problems
- added small graphics
- fixed small issues
- fixed problems taking the dynamite, climbing the pole and speaking to the officer, on some few resolutions
